rationale: Evaluating omission of required braking requires characterising both the need for braking and whether the vehicle actually initiates it. The braking response itself therefore belongs to P. H-1 and FR-7 establish its collision-avoidance purpose, while H-1 and FR-7.1 support including timeliness of braking. The declared operational situation matches H-1, and P does not incorporate the internal observation, computation, or communication mechanisms used to produce the response.
determining_elements: “Whether a braking maneuver is required” identifies the condition necessary to evaluate SG-1's prohibition on omitting required braking.
“Whether braking is actually initiated” identifies the vehicle behaviour directly required by SG-1 and FR-7.
“In time to avoid collision” is supported by H-1's failure to stop in time and FR-7.1's braking-onset requirement; it is not merely an imported sensing deadline.
The specified road, speed, weather, and pedestrian encounter reproduce H-1's operational situation.
The scoped “braking/avoidance response” corresponds to FR-7's braking maneuver to avoid collisions.
